features.title: Capture anything and let it sort itself
features.summary: One capture box and one agent tool take free text; kind, title, tags and links (items, threads, jj revisions, branches, URLs) are derived from it, and an agent capture links its thread and project.
failureModes: An unknown prefix stays in the title and the item becomes a task.
A storage write failure is logged and the in-memory item stays readable.

features.title: Feed ordered by activity, with idle items sinking
features.summary: The feed lists pinned items, then newest activity first. Status chips narrow the feed and the Items list to one status or several at once. Freshness is derived on read: notes go dormant after 14 days, other open items after 30, idle in-progress work is flagged stale, closed items archive after 7 days; any touch revives an item.
failureModes: Dormant and archived items stay in search and backlinks; only the default feed hides them.

verification.testName: shows every status until a chip is picked, then only the picked ones

hides dormant items from the feed until something touches them

features.title: Rename an item in place
features.summary: Double-clicking an item in the feed, an Items row or a board card swaps its title for an inline editor; Enter or a click elsewhere saves, Escape leaves the item untouched, and the quick gesture never opens the peek or card detail.
failureModes: An unchanged, blank or escape-cancelled draft closes the editor without a Host write.
A double click on a link, chip or button inside the row keeps that control's own action instead of starting a rename.

features.title: Board, links, backlinks and history
features.summary: A board groups the same items into Inbox, Todo, In progress, Done and Dropped columns in that order. Titles and descriptions render Markdown and URLs as clickable links in the feed, board and detail. An item's detail links it to threads, revisions, branches, workspaces, URLs or other items, lists the items that link to it, and shows every event with its actor; fields the user set are recorded as theirs.
failureModes: An unknown item id answers not-found without writing.

verification.testName: records who moved an item and which fields the user owns
answers backlinks for items and for any linked target

features.title: Select items in ranges and batch-edit them
features.summary: The Items table supports click-to-open, Shift-click ranges, Cmd/Ctrl-click additive toggles, select-all-visible, batch status, kind and pin updates, and one thread for the whole selection from the action bar or the row's context menu.
failureModes: A range uses the current visible item order and falls back to the target if its anchor is no longer visible.

features.title: Triage new items automatically
features.summary: With autoTriage on, each capture is triaged in the background: Jev answers whether it is work to do and whether it repeats the closest open item, a configured cheap model proposes kind, status, title, tags and duplicates using the user's past corrections as examples. A confident proposal applies as `system` and skips fields the user set by hand; a hesitant one waits on the item to be accepted or dismissed.
failureModes: A failing or missing Jev key or model is skipped; the item stays in the Inbox.
A model answer with invalid fields keeps only the valid ones; a duplicate it was not shown is ignored.

features.title: Backfill triage on items captured before it was set up
features.summary: Triage only runs on capture, so the wand in the panel header backfills it: the oldest open items no triage has looked at yet, 25 per run, one at a time. The dialog reports what it applied, left as suggestions, found unchanged and how many items remain, so a second run continues where it stopped. An agent runs the same pass with backlog_triage_backfill, optionally re-triaging items triage already looked at or including closed ones.

features.title: Move items from thread and revision signals
features.summary: A user message mentioning b:<n> links that thread and starts the item; a revision on main whose description says Closes/Fixes/Resolves b:<n> links the revision and finishes it; a linked thread whose turn ended blocked or failed flags its open items as blocked until a finished turn clears that same flag; with threadResolution on, Jev reads a finished reply and leaves a Done suggestion on the items it resolved, never a silent close. Signals only move forward and never over a status or attention the user set by hand.
failureModes: A repository without jj or a main bookmark is skipped.
An unchanged main costs one read-only jj call and is not rescanned.
A cancelled, token-ceiling or crash-interrupted turn leaves the linked items alone.
A missing Jev key, a failing call or a reply that only reports progress suggests nothing.

externalDependencies.boundary: Read-only `jj log --ignore-working-copy` on main in the repositories open items name (and revisionRepositories), bounded output and a 20s timeout.

features.title: A chat-sized capture box with files, properties and references
features.summary: The composer is a three-line card with a Linear-style toolbar: `+` adds an image or any file, or links a backlog item or a thread; the project chip picks the item's project (see project-scope); status and kind chips are editable before sending; images can be pasted, dropped or picked, are scaled in the browser, other files keep their bytes, and all are kept with the item; the microphone records through the Host voice-input bundle and inserts the transcript into the same draft. Images render as a thumbnail grid, other files as download rows, and feed cards show a paperclip count; clicking any image opens the same keyboard-navigable gallery as the thread composer, both for pending attachments and for the images kept with an item.

features.title: Start a thread from an item
features.summary: Clicking a board card opens the item detail beside the board. Right-clicking an item in the feed, Inbox, Items, Board, Projects, search results, or its detail view opens the same actions: start a linked thread; change status, kind, attention or project; pin or unpin; run triage; or open the item. Starting a thread picks the item project, account/model and effort, and an opening message; the row selected in the Items table starts a thread for the whole selection, every item is linked and named in the opening message, and the thread is created in its own jj workspace of that project, named and linked, sending immediately unless configured to keep an editable draft. The dialog closes as soon as it hands the request over, so the panel never waits for the workspace; the banner says the work is under way, the thread opens only when the dialog's open box, or the startThreadOpensCreated setting, asks for it, and the report carries an Open action otherwise. The Host verb behind it is the tool `backlog_start_thread`, so an agent starts the same thread without redirecting its own caller.

expect text "Start a thread from b:1"
expect checkbox "Open the thread when it is created"
